items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1971-07-09
items.q: The mention of 'King Rex' is part of an anecdote narrated by the INTERVIEWER about Louis Armstrong's behavior in England; the interviewee (Louis Armstrong) does not interact with or claim a personal relationship with the figure of King Rex.

ctx.x: Thank you. Hello, Dolly. Another example. Saints go marching in, and Louis almost always... This recall...

We're real proud of the fact that he was born and raised in New Orleans. The central figure in the Mardi Gras here in New Orleans is King Rex, who is the king of the parade on Mardi Gras Day, the Rex parade. So when Louis Armstrong had an opportunity to play for royalty in England, he addressed the royal box, the king and the queen of England. When he was ready to play his last tune, the saints go marching in. And he said to the king, he said, this next number is for you, Rex. That gives you an idea of the kind…

Oh, when the saints go marching in, Yes, I want to be in that number when the saints go marching in. Yes, I want to be in that number when the saints go marching in. Oh, when the saints go marching in, And when the saints go marching in, Who can doubt that number? I was Louis Armstrong when I was 15 years old, When I was an office boy at Associated Booking Corporation. I was his road manager, who about seven years later, He was the kindest human being I've ever met in my life. He was always happy, and he wanted…
